title: Joins & Set Operations
tagline: tables connecting — the Venn diagram of data

options: Only left table has a match
Only right table has a match
placementQuiz.explain: INNER JOIN = intersection. Only rows with matches in both tables.

options: All left rows, matched right or NULL
Only left rows with no match
All right rows, matched left or NULL

placementQuiz.q: SELECT * FROM a JOIN b ON a.id = b.id is equivalent to:
options: SELECT * FROM a, b WHERE a.id = b.id
SELECT * FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON a.id = b.id
SELECT * FROM a FULL JOIN b ON a.id = b.id
SELECT * FROM a CROSS JOIN b
placementQuiz.explain: Comma join with WHERE = INNER JOIN. Explicit JOIN syntax preferred.

options: UNION removes duplicates; UNION ALL keeps all
placementQuiz.explain: UNION = distinct (sorts/removes dups). UNION ALL = all rows, faster.

placementQuiz.q: JOIN condition in WHERE vs ON for LEFT JOIN:
options: WHERE filters after join (can turn LEFT into INNER)
placementQuiz.explain: ON filters before preserving left rows. WHERE filters after — can eliminate NULL-extended rows.

blocks.md: A JOIN connects two tables on a common column. Think Venn diagrams: INNER = intersection, LEFT = left circle + overlap, FULL = both circles.
Every row in employees has a dept_id pointing to departments. JOIN follows that pointer to bring department info into the employee row. It's like looking up a phone number in a directory.

items: Primary key (PK) = unique identifier in parent table (departments.id)
Foreign key (FK) = pointer in child table (employees.dept_id)

sections.title: Inner & Left Joins — The Core Two

blocks.label: inner join
blocks.code:
-- Explicit syntax (preferred)
SELECT e.name, d.name AS department
FROM employees e
INNER JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id;

-- Implicit (old style, avoid)
SELECT e.name, d.name
FROM employees e, departments d
WHERE e.dept_id = d.id;
blocks.py-pandas:
# Inner join (default)
merged = employees.merge(departments, left_on='dept_id', right_on='id', how='inner')

# Suffixes for overlapping columns
merged = employees.merge(departments, left_on='dept_id', right_on='id', 
                         how='inner', suffixes=('_emp', '_dept'))
blocks.py-sqlalchemy:
# Explicit join
session.query(Employee.name, Department.name.label('department'))
    .join(Department, Employee.dept_id == Department.id).all()

blocks.label: left join
blocks.code:
-- All employees, even those without department
SELECT e.name, d.name AS department
FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id;
-- Employees with no dept: d.name = NULL

-- Find employees WITHOUT department
SELECT e.name
FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id
WHERE d.id IS NULL;
blocks.py-pandas:
# Left join
merged = employees.merge(departments, left_on='dept_id', right_on='id', how='left')

# Find NULLs (no match)
no_dept = merged[merged['name_dept'].isna()]['name_emp']
blocks.py-sqlalchemy:
# Left join
session.query(Employee.name, Department.name.label('department'))
    .outerjoin(Department, Employee.dept_id == Department.id).all()

# No match
session.query(Employee.name).outerjoin(Department)
    .filter(Department.id.is_(None)).all()

items.q: LEFT JOIN with 10 left rows, 3 matches → result rows:
items.explain: LEFT JOIN returns all left rows (10). 3 matched, 7 NULL-extended.

items.q: WHERE d.id IS NULL after LEFT JOIN finds:
items.explain: NULL-extended rows = no match in right table. Classic anti-join pattern.

blocks.label: right join
blocks.code:
-- All departments, even those with no employees
SELECT d.name, e.name AS employee
FROM employees e
RIGHT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id;
-- Departments with no employees: e.name = NULL
blocks.py-pandas:
# Right join
merged = employees.merge(departments, left_on='dept_id', right_on='id', how='right')
blocks.py-sqlalchemy:
# Right join
session.query(Department.name, Employee.name)
    .join(Employee, Department.id == Employee.dept_id, isouter=True).all()

blocks.label: full join
blocks.code:
-- All employees AND all departments
SELECT e.name, d.name
FROM employees e
FULL JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id;
-- Matched rows + NULL-extended left + NULL-extended right
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL: no FULL JOIN
-- Correct workaround: LEFT JOIN + anti-join on right
SELECT * FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id
UNION ALL
SELECT * FROM employees e RIGHT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id
WHERE e.dept_id IS NULL;
blocks.py-pandas:
# Full outer join
merged = employees.merge(departments, left_on='dept_id', right_on='id', how='outer')
blocks.py-sqlalchemy:
# Full outer join
session.query(Employee.name, Department.name)
    .outerjoin(Department, Employee.dept_id == Department.id, full=True).all()

blocks.label: self join (manager lookup)
blocks.code:
-- Employee + their manager name
SELECT e.name AS employee, m.name AS manager
FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id;
-- Same table, different aliases (e and m)
blocks.py-pandas:
# Self merge
merged = employees.merge(employees, left_on='manager_id', right_on='id', 
                         how='left', suffixes=('_emp', '_mgr'))
blocks.py-sqlalchemy:
# Self join
m = aliased(Employee)
session.query(Employee.name, m.name.label('manager'))
    .outerjoin(m, Employee.manager_id == m.id).all()

items.q: FULL JOIN vs LEFT JOIN UNION ALL RIGHT JOIN (anti-join):
options: FULL JOIN equals LEFT UNION RIGHT (UNION removes dups)
FULL JOIN = LEFT UNION ALL RIGHT WHERE right.key IS NULL
They are never equivalent in any database system
items.explain: FULL JOIN preserves all rows from both sides. LEFT UNION RIGHT with UNION removes duplicates (wrong). Correct workaround: LEFT JOIN UNION ALL RIGHT JOIN with anti-join filter (WHERE left.key IS NULL) to avoid duplicating matched rows.

options: Two physical copies of the table
A UNION of the table with itself
items.explain: The table appears twice in FROM, so aliases (e1, e2) are what tell the two copies apart. A self-referencing FK such as manager_id -> emp_id is the classic join condition, but it is not required: you can self-join on any condition, e.g. two employees in the same city.

sections.title: Worked Problem — Employees With Departments (Anti-Join Pattern)

blocks.text: Problem: Find departments with no employees

blocks.md: We need departments that have zero employees. This is the classic anti-join pattern — find rows in the parent table with no matching child rows.

blocks.label: sample data
blocks.code:
-- departments
 dept_id | dept_name  | location
--------+------------+----------
      1 | Executive  | Mumbai
      2 | Engineering| Bengaluru
      7 | Research   | Hyderabad  -- no employees

-- employees (only 3 shown)
 emp_id | name   | dept_id
--------+--------+--------
      1 | Anita  | 1
      2 | Vikram | 2
      5 | Priya  | 2

blocks.label: Brute: NOT IN subquery
blocks.code:
SELECT dept_name FROM departments
WHERE dept_id NOT IN (SELECT dept_id FROM employees);

blocks.label: Optimal: LEFT JOIN + WHERE IS NULL
blocks.code:
SELECT d.dept_name
FROM departments d
LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id
WHERE e.emp_id IS NULL;
blocks.py-pandas:
merged = departments.merge(employees, left_on='dept_id', right_on='dept_id', how='left', indicator=True)
result = merged[merged['_merge'] == 'left_only'][['dept_name']]

blocks.title: Anti-Join Dry Run (LEFT JOIN + WHERE IS NULL)

stages.label: FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e
stages.sql: SELECT d.dept_id, d.dept_name, e.emp_id FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id
stages.note: All 7 departments preserved. Research (dept_id=7) gets NULL for emp_id.

stages.label: WHERE e.emp_id IS NULL
stages.sql: SELECT d.dept_name FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id WHERE e.emp_id IS NULL
stages.note: Filters to only Research (dept_id=7) — the department with no employees.

blocks.md: Optimal approach uses LEFT JOIN + IS NULL. The planner turns this into a Hash Anti Join — single pass, no NULL trap. Brute NOT IN fails silently if employees.dept_id has NULLs.

sections.title: Trap — LEFT JOIN + WHERE on Right Side Turns It Into INNER JOIN

blocks.claim: Adding a WHERE condition on the right table after a LEFT JOIN is safe — it just filters the result.
blocks.refutation: FALSE. A WHERE clause on the right table's columns (e.g., `WHERE d.location = 'Mumbai'`) filters AFTER the join, eliminating NULL-extended rows. This converts your LEFT JOIN into an INNER JOIN.
blocks.correctModel: Keep right-table filters in the ON clause for LEFT JOIN. Only use WHERE for left-table filters or for the anti-join pattern (WHERE right.pk IS NULL).

evidence.label: The trap in action
evidence.code:
-- WRONG: WHERE on right table kills LEFT JOIN
SELECT e.name, d.name
FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id
WHERE d.location = 'Mumbai';  -- Loses employees with NULL dept!

-- CORRECT: filter in ON clause
SELECT e.name, d.name
FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id AND d.location = 'Mumbai';
evidence.pg:
-- EXPLAIN shows Hash Right Join + Filter for wrong version
-- Correct version: Hash Right Join with join filter

blocks.label: union / intersect / except
blocks.code:
-- UNION: all distinct rows from both
SELECT name FROM employees
UNION
SELECT name FROM contractors;
-- Removes duplicates

-- UNION ALL: all rows, keep duplicates
SELECT name FROM employees
UNION ALL
SELECT name FROM contractors;
-- Faster, no dedup

-- INTERSECT: common rows
SELECT dept_id FROM employees
INTERSECT
SELECT id FROM departments;

-- EXCEPT: in first, not in second
SELECT dept_id FROM departments
EXCEPT
SELECT dept_id FROM employees;
-- Departments with NO employees
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL 8.0+: INTERSECT, EXCEPT supported
-- Older: use EXISTS/NOT EXISTS
blocks.py-pandas:
# Union
pd.concat([employees['name'], contractors['name']]).drop_duplicates()

# Union all
pd.concat([employees['name'], contractors['name']])

# Intersect
set(employees['dept_id']) & set(departments['id'])

# Except
set(departments['id']) - set(employees['dept_id'])
blocks.py-sqlalchemy:
# Union
from sqlalchemy import union, union_all
q1 = session.query(Employee.name)
q2 = session.query(Contractor.name)
session.query(union(q1, q2)).all()

# Intersect/Except
from sqlalchemy import intersect, except_
session.query(intersect(...)).all()

options: UNION ALL is faster (no dedup step)
items.explain: UNION ALL skips sort/unique. Use when duplicates OK or impossible.

items.q: EXCEPT is to NOT IN as INTERSECT is to:
items.explain: EXCEPT = in first not in second. INTERSECT = in both = IN logic.

approaches.name: Brute
approaches.idea: Comma join with WHERE clause (old syntax)
approaches.code: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, d.dept_name FROM employees e, departments d WHERE e.dept_id = d.dept_id ORDER BY e.emp_id

approaches.cost: Hash Join or Merge Join depending on indexes; clear intent

items.title: All Employees + Department (Include No Dept)
items.statement: List all employees (first_name, last_name) with their department dept_name. Include employees without a department (show NULL for dept_name). Order by employee emp_id.
hints: LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id

exercise.solution: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, d.dept_name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id ORDER BY e.emp_id

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: LEFT JOIN preserves all left rows
approaches.code: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, d.dept_name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id ORDER BY e.emp_id
approaches.cost: Single scan + hash join; NULLs handled automatically
approaches.pitfalls: None — this is what LEFT JOIN is for

items.title: Departments Without Employees
items.statement: Find departments that have no employees. Return dept_name only. Use the anti-join pattern (LEFT JOIN + WHERE right.pk IS NULL).
hints: LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id

exercise.solution: SELECT d.dept_name FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id WHERE e.emp_id IS NULL

approaches.name: Brute
approaches.code: SELECT dept_name FROM departments WHERE dept_id NOT IN (SELECT dept_id FROM employees)
approaches.cost: Subquery scan + filter; fails silently if subquery has NULLs
approaches.pitfalls: NULL in subquery returns zero rows — silent bug

approaches.name: Better
approaches.code: SELECT d.dept_name FROM departments d WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees e WHERE e.dept_id = d.dept_id)
approaches.cost: Semi-join optimization; stops at first match per department
approaches.pitfalls: Slightly more verbose than LEFT JOIN

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.code: SELECT d.dept_name FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id WHERE e.emp_id IS NULL
approaches.cost: Hash Anti Join — single pass, no NULL trap, planner optimizes well
approaches.pitfalls: Must use PK column in IS NULL check (emp_id not dept_id)

items.statement: List each employee's first_name, last_name with their manager's first_name, last_name. Include employees without a manager (show NULL). Order by employee emp_id.

Select e.first_name, e.last_name, m.first_name AS mgr_first, m.last_name AS mgr_last

exercise.solution: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, m.first_name AS mgr_first, m.last_name AS mgr_last FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id ORDER BY e.emp_id

items.statement: Combine all department names (dept_name) and distinct job titles (job_title) into a single column 'name'. Remove duplicates. Order by name.
hints: Use UNION (not UNION ALL) to remove duplicates

exercise.solution: SELECT dept_name AS name FROM departments UNION SELECT DISTINCT job_title FROM employees ORDER BY name

revisionCard: INNER = intersection; LEFT = all left + match; RIGHT = all right + match; FULL = both
LEFT JOIN + WHERE right.id IS NULL = anti-join (left rows with no match)
JOIN condition in ON, not WHERE (especially for LEFT — WHERE filters after join)
Self join = table aliases + FK to same table (manager_id → id)
UNION = distinct (slow); UNION ALL = all rows (fast); use ALL when possible
INTERSECT = common; EXCEPT = in first not second

glossary.def: Returns only rows with matches in both tables (intersection).
All left rows; matched right rows or NULL (left circle + overlap).
All right rows; matched left rows or NULL (right circle + overlap).
All rows from both tables; NULLs where no match (union of circles).
Table joined to itself using aliases; FK references same table PK.
LEFT JOIN + WHERE right.key IS NULL — finds rows with no match.
